exposure: cervical dilatation >= 6 cm at the time of CS
cohort: The study included 94 Thai postpartum women who had undergone at least one Cesarean section and were examined at six weeks postpartum.
finding: The overall prevalence of large CSD was 22.3%, and repeated CS, uterine retroflexion, and cervical dilatation >= 6 cm at the time of CS were significantly associated with higher odds of developing a large CSD.
mod_finding: Repeated Cesarean section was a significant factor associated with a large CSD, with women in the repeat CS group having a 36.7% prevalence of large CSD compared to 15.6% in the primary CS group.
